gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.
'Especially' means in particular or above all; 'specially' means for one particular purpose.

gaps.sentence: The hospital is ___ the city centre.
gaps.explanation: 'Near' is a preposition before a place; 'nearly' is an adverb of degree meaning almost; 'close' needs 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to choose ___ the two options.
gaps.explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for a group of more than two.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).
